parts.note: a litter is a carried chair; the clue wants one that shares its name with an 1870 battle of the Franco-Prussian War

explanation.surface: A question about the debris or rubbish left on a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' suggests rubbish strewn over a battlefield, but here it is a covered chair carried on poles, and the battle is the French town where Napoleon III surrendered in 1870.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is a kind of litter, and Sedan is the site of a famous 1870 battle.

parts.note: to back a proposal is to second it
a train or string is a series of things in a line, such as a string of racehorses

explanation.surface: Reservists are heading back for more training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserves' reads as a verb or as soldiers, but it is the sports sense: the second-choice players.
explanation.definitionFit: A team's second string is its reserve players, those picked after the first choices.

clue.text: Morally obliged by loyalty to Bob

parts.note: loyalty is a sense of duty owed to someone
to bob is to move up and down with a jump, as does a bound

explanation.surface: Someone feels honour-bound because of their loyalty to a friend called Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name but is the verb, to bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: Being duty-bound means being required by conscience or obligation to act.

indicators.note: in tells us the point goes inside the name of the resort

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A family member with a holiday spot on the Côte d'Azur.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a relative of the family.

parts.note: a Parsi is a follower of Zoroastrianism, mainly in India
a flower is something that flows, i.e. a river; the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A Zoroastrian flower that is also an opera, as if a bloom were named for a stage work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword's river (something that flows); the Fal is a Cornish river.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's final music drama is a well-known opera about the Grail knight.

clue.text: River Plate's no place for beginner retrained as a proper pirate

indicators.note: retrained suggests the remaining letters are put through a new routine, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: no place for says one letter is excluded from the river's name

parts.note: the River Plate is the estuary between Argentina and Uruguay; the 's stands for is
L stands for learner, a beginner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: The River Plate is said to be no place for a novice who has retrained as a real buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no place for' removes L (beginner) from PLATE, leaving PATE; with RIVER, 'retrained' rearranges RIVERPATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was a privately owned ship or captain licensed by a government to attack enemy shipping, a pirate with official papers.

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: deer are animals

explanation.surface: Livestock reared on pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns DEER upwards to read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass growing in wet places.

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters are made new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A character inheriting something in a book by the vet-author James Herriot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book by James Herriot, the Yorkshire vet-author, but it is the signal to rearrange the surname's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir who receives property under a will is its beneficiary.

definitions.meaning: popular without U (the crossword's upper-class or posh letter) leaves poplar, and the white poplar has this name
the white poplar is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree that is well liked but not upmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Take U (posh, as in U and non-U) out of POPULAR to get POPLAR; this answer is the white poplar, so both halves point to the same tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar, a European tree with silvery leaves.

clue.text: Girl's turn, which may produce a sparkling performance

definitions.text: which may produce a sparkling performance

parts.note: Catherine is a girl's name
to wheel is to turn round

explanation.surface: A girl takes her turn and puts on a dazzling show.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('has'), joining the girl to her turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning firework that throws off sparks is named after St Catherine's wheel, a sparkling display.

clue.text: Even a large quantity ends up as a fair bargain

parts.note: even or straight means honest and level
a deal of something, as in a good deal, is a large quantity

explanation.surface: A large amount of something, evened out, comes out as an honest transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight deal is an honest, fair arrangement between parties.

parts.note: noble means fine or splendid
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Someone gazes at a splendid work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' reads as a verb, to look closely, but is the noun: a member of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the realm is a titled aristocrat, a lord.

clue.text: Burning to provide dramatist with model

parts.note: John Arden was an English playwright
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T is a model

explanation.surface: Someone eager to supply a playwright with a sitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate, burning with feeling; it comes from the Latin for burning.

clue.text: Shield displaying rabbit's tail — church has one, possibly

parts.note: a scut is the short tail of a rabbit, hare or deer

indicators.note: possibly says the word one may appear in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A coat of arms showing a rabbit's tail, which a church might own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ONE to EON; 'displaying' and 'has' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A scutcheon is an escutcheon, the shield bearing a coat of arms.

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
to institute something is to found or establish it

explanation.surface: Conservatives defeat establishments, a political news line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'institutes' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound an enemy or a plan is to defeat or thwart it.

parts.note: nick is slang for prison, so names given to inmates there could be called this; ordinarily it means pet names or informal names

explanation.surface: A question about how inmates are addressed.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'the nick' is prison; the question mark flags the pun on informal names.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal or pet names used in place of real names are what one calls people, and inmates of the nick bear names.

definitions.meaning: a reed pipe played in ancient Rome and Greece

explanation.surface: An old pipe carved out of bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the Latin name of an old flute and the anatomical name for the shinbone.

clue.text: Nitric ban adapted for the British

indicators.note: adapted says the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A ban on nitric acid modified to suit people in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges NITRICBAN; 'for the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannic is a formal word for British, as in Her Britannic Majesty.

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps
Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology

explanation.surface: Someone who carved a statue of a river deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker.

definitions.meaning: ..., tying up with cord once more
the act of putting sound on tape

explanation.surface: Tying something up a second time with sticky tape.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits as RE-CORDING; the question mark admits the tape is audio, not adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: Recording means capturing sound on tape, and read as two parts it means tying with cord again.

clue.text: Thought it over in midday break

indicators.note: in says the reversed word goes inside the time of day

parts.note: noon is midday

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone mulled things over during their lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' is a link: the midday word is broken open to take the reversed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or thought.

clue.text: Novice in row with ceramic worker

indicators.note: in says the beginner's letter goes inside the word for a row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
L stands for learner, a novice

explanation.surface: A beginner sits in a line alongside a potter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler lays ceramic tiles, so is a worker in ceramics.

indicators.note: catching says one word grabs and holds the other inside

parts.note: intact means undamaged, unhurt
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone escapes harm while catching a thief caught in the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught in the act means caught red-handed, during the wrongdoing.

clue.text: Sixth or seventh part of an animal

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fraction, a sixth or a seventh, of some creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse is a large domesticated animal.

clue.text: The lady's large figure or divine bust

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman, the lady's
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large figure

explanation.surface: A woman's ample figure or a heavenly bosom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large figure' is not a body shape but a big number, M (1000).
explanation.definitionFit: A herm is a pillar topped with a bust of a god, originally Hermes.

parts.note: fruit of battle suggests the spoils of victory, but the clue wants an apple variety named after a 1704 battle site and Oxfordshire palace

explanation.surface: A question about what a victory yields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit' suggests the rewards of war; it is a real apple, named after Blenheim, Marlborough's 1704 victory and the palace in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old English apple variety named after Blenheim, the battle and the estate.

clue.text: Thinks of journalists surrounding, say, you and me

indicators.note: surrounding says the reporters' word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: the press means journalists collectively

indicators.note: say tells us the word is pronounced, giving a single letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the letter U sounds like the word you
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reporters gathered round people like us form their assumptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you and me' looks like the pronoun us, but 'say' makes 'you' the single letter that sounds like it, as in text speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to suppose or take for granted, which is to think something without proof.

clue.text: Forty letters are said to stand out

indicators.note: are said tells us the letters are spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals, two letters

explanation.surface: Forty letters are reported to be outstanding, as if a postbag were remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, X and L sound like 'ex-ell'.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be outstanding, to stand out from others.
